lead.headline: An Indian is among two killed in a Houthi attack on Dammam's airport, and the US orders non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia
lead.short: Two people, a Saudi and an Indian, were killed and eight injured when Houthi forces attacked King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on Wednesday night, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said. The Indian embassy said two more Indians were among the injured. Hours later the US State Department ordered non-emergency staff and their families to leave the kingdom.

why.text: Millions of Indians live and work in Saudi Arabia, and the attacks on its airports and oil fields keep crude above $110 a barrel.

more: The aviation authority raised its count from one dead to two. AFP counts 22 people killed in attacks on Saudi airports this month. A drone was also aimed at the Shaybah oil field, though reports differ on whether anyone died there.

The State Department said the hostilities "have the potential to escalate rapidly" and told Americans to reconsider travel. The truce between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis collapsed in July, and the Houthis have since declared a blockade of Saudi shipping.
A Kuwait-flagged tanker carrying 21 Indian seafarers was also hit in the Strait of Hormuz; all of them are safe.

update.new: An Indian is killed in an attack on Dammam's airport, and the US orders its non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia.
update.front: The Houthi war on Saudi Arabia has now killed an Indian, and Washington is pulling its staff out.

seconds.headline: Governments take websites offline as two PHP flaws found with AI help put most of the web at risk
seconds.short: Two serious security flaws in PHP, the language behind most of the world's websites, have pushed governments in Europe and Asia to take sites offline. The pair, called PHP2Shell, were found with the help of AI models. The NSA, Britain's National Cyber Security Centre and CERT-EU have issued rare warnings, and site owners are told to update now.

why.text: PHP runs WordPress, Drupal and Wikipedia's software, so an unpatched flaw reaches a huge share of the sites people use every day.

more: Researchers at the security firm Calif, working with OpenAI, reported the first flaw on 11 August, and Wiz, owned by Alphabet, reported the second on 24 August. OpenAI called it "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory". Wiz says PHP powers about 70% of the world's websites, including those built on WordPress, Joomla, Drupal and MediaWiki.
The PHP Foundation said the flaws are among the most severe it has dealt with and urged everyone to install the patched versions released this week. The first is listed as CVE-2026-109618.

Authorities in Europe, Asia and elsewhere took some government websites offline while they patched. PHP, created in 1995, assembles the pages a server sends to browsers, and runs content management systems, social media sites and online shops.

seconds.headline: Putin agrees in principle to restart three-way peace talks after a three-hour meeting with Witkoff, and Abu Dhabi is floated for November
seconds.short: Russia is "ready in principle" to resume three-way peace talks with Ukraine and the US, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said after Vladimir Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg for about three hours on Wednesday. A new round could take place in Abu Dhabi around 10 November. Donald Trump said this was "maybe now the closest we've been".

why.text: The talks stopped in February, and this is the first time since then that both sides have named a place and a rough date to meet.

more: Witkoff, with Jared Kushner also involved, saw Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo on Tuesday before flying to Russia. Ushakov said some of the American ideas were not very "useful", and gave no sign that Moscow had softened its demands. Russia holds about 20% of Ukraine.
The fighting went on through the visit. Kyiv's mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said six people were injured in a Russian missile attack on the capital.

Zelensky said strong security guarantees for Ukraine and an energy ceasefire were discussed in Oslo. Ushakov said any new talks must focus on "building a security system" for Russia and Ukraine. Moscow blamed Ukrainian strikes during its general elections last month for disrupting the last rounds.

facts.meeting: Putin and Witkoff, St Petersburg, Wed, about three hours

update.new: Putin met Witkoff and agreed in principle to restart three-way talks, possibly in Abu Dhabi around 10 November.
update.front: It is the first date and place for Ukraine peace talks since they stopped in February.

seconds.headline: A New Mexico judge orders Meta to pay $25bn over privacy violations dating to Cambridge Analytica, the largest penalty it has faced
seconds.short: A judge in New Mexico has ordered Meta to pay $25bn (£18.6bn) after a two-week trial over how Facebook handled its users' data, the biggest penalty the company has faced. The case grew out of the Cambridge Analytica scandal, and the jury found Meta broke state law more than 40 million times, affecting about two million residents.

why.text: The sum dwarfs earlier privacy fines, and other US states can bring similar cases under their own consumer laws.

more: Meta's lawyer CJ Mahoney said the ruling would make it "all but impossible to do business in the state", and the company says it will appeal. New Mexico's attorney general, Raúl Torrez, said the verdict showed that "no corporation is too powerful" to be held to account.
Earlier this year Meta agreed an $18bn settlement with California over child safety on its platforms. The New Mexico penalty is larger than any fine the company has paid to US or European regulators.

The state argued that Meta executives had said for years that user data was never shared with third parties without permission, when it had been. Mahoney said the lawsuit "seeks to impose a tax on speech".

seconds.headline: The Nifty falls 0.9% by 2pm, a third day of losses, as Brent climbs past $112 on the Saudi attacks
seconds.short: Indian shares fell for a third day on Thursday, with the Nifty 50 down 0.9% at about 22,616 by 2pm and the Sensex down 0.6% at about 73,262. Brent crude rose more than 3% to about $112 a barrel after the Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, and 15 of 16 main sectors opened lower.

why.text: India buys most of its oil abroad, so every rise in crude feeds inflation and squeezes the government's budget.

more: Small and mid-sized companies fell harder, each index down 1.3% in early trade. Capital goods makers led the losses, with Gallantt Ispat down 12%, Ramkrishna Forgings 10% and KEI Industries 8%. Minutes of the RBI's last policy meeting suggest more rate rises may be needed to hold down prices.

On Wednesday the Nifty closed down 0.34% at 22,811.35, having recovered about 124 points after 2pm. IT shares have regained about ₹3.87 lakh crore in value this month, and foreign investors bought ₹6,463 crore of them in the September quarter, though the Nifty IT index fell 1.6% on Thursday. TCS has gained 23% in October and Infosys 17%.

update.new: A third day of losses as oil climbs on the Saudi attacks.
update.front: The attacks in Saudi Arabia have reached Indian savings: oil is above $112 and shares are falling for a third day.

stories.headline: CJP leaders Das and Ranka are freed on bonds and summoned by the Crime Branch, as Amit Shah says the protests 'will not achieve anything'
stories.short: CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released on Wednesday after a Special Executive Magistrate accepted bonds of ₹50,000 each. They undertook not to call protests at Jantar Mantar until its denotification, and Delhi Police's Crime Branch summoned both to its Rajouri Garden office on Thursday. Their next hearing is on Friday afternoon.

why.text: The government has now answered the protests over the voter roll revision directly, while the police keep pressing the movement's leaders.

more: The two were detained over the 13 October protest at Jantar Mantar. Home Minister Amit Shah, at the launch of 33 Delhi Jal Board projects worth ₹8,941 crore, said, "These protests and demonstrations will not achieve anything," and accused the protesters' backers: "you want to save the votes of infiltrators".
The economist Parakala Prabhakar will join CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke at an anti-SIR march in Delhi on Friday.

Police allege the two entered the protest area through private premises and broke conditions on keeping the peace. The magistrate asked the investigating officer to verify their sureties by the next hearing, and told Das, Ranka and their sureties to attend.

update.new: Das and Ranka are released on bonds and summoned by the Crime Branch; Amit Shah speaks against the protests.

stories.headline: Como beat Manchester United 4–1, extending their run without a win to seven games, as Carrick says the display is 'not acceptable'
stories.short: Manchester United lost 4–1 to Como on Wednesday, with Nico Paz scoring in the second minute and the Italian side leading 4–0 before Joshua Zirkzee's late consolation. United have gone seven games without a win, their worst start in 40 years. Michael Carrick called the performance "not acceptable" but said he had not thought about his own position.

why.text: United's poor run has turned into an open row between the captain and the manager, which rarely ends well for the manager.

more: "I have not given my own position any thought," Carrick said after the game. Captain Bruno Fernandes had questioned his tactics in a television interview, and Youri Tielemans said "everything was missing".

Jamie Carragher called Fernandes's public criticism of his manager an "absolute disgrace" and said a captain should keep such complaints inside the dressing room. Carrick has been in charge since the start of the season.

Cesc Fàbregas's Como had lost 2–0 to Atlético Madrid last week. Carrick said the display was "the total opposite" of the one at Leeds and "tough to watch". "It's difficult to understand how it can be so different," he said.

update.new: A 4–1 defeat at Como and a public row between Fernandes and Carrick.

stories.headline: Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4–1 for a third straight Champions League win, with Bernardo Silva scoring his first goal for the club
stories.short: Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4–1 at the Bernabéu on Wednesday night to make it three wins from three in the Champions League, with nine points. Bernardo Silva scored his first Madrid goal just before half-time, Arda Güler added a second after the break, and Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande scored late either side of a Leipzig reply.

why.text: Madrid go to Barcelona on Sunday with their European group well in hand and their best players rested in parts.

more: Silva opened the scoring in the 44th minute and Güler made it 2–0 in the 52nd. Mbappé scored in the 83rd minute, Gomis pulled one back for Leipzig two minutes later and Diomande restored the three-goal lead in the 87th.

Federico Valverde, at right-back, was Managing Madrid's best player with a 9 rating and 116 touches. Thibaut Courtois made five saves and earned an 8.5, while Álvaro Carreras struggled and got a 5. Güler, rated 9, set up Silva's goal, and Vinícius, rated 6.5, was whistled by part of the Bernabéu.
Madrid play the Clásico at Camp Nou on Sunday at 01:30 IST on Monday, without the suspended Vinícius Júnior.
